summary: Publish measured standby source database sizes and their enforced limit, and warn before bounded RAM scratch is exhausted.

verification.observed: PR 689 passed both primary checks, merged as 15480f8fa6465598af528c586a56b2f07a73091f, and merged-main pipeline 2430 passed. Courier, receiver and drill tests passed.

The primary Prometheus promtool validated all rules and simulated healthy, warning, critical, recovery, and missing-telemetry cases. Separate transaction fixtures verified sender and rule installation plus owned rollback.
At 17:25 UTC the sender and unit were installed under the existing courier flock with private before-images. The timer remained active and the service was not restarted.

The 17:26 UTC scheduled run verified both standby databases, published source sizes 121667584 and 223035392 bytes against a 469762048-byte limit, and removed its runtime directory. The five-minute encrypted job verified both replicas.
At 17:27 UTC the primary Prometheus scraped both source sizes and loaded the warning, critical and missing-telemetry rules healthy; the original rule file was preserved in a private backup.

limitations: The warning depends on the primary Prometheus scrape; the standby Prometheus does not currently scrape this courier.
A database can grow past the hard limit between scheduled observations; failed or missing copies retain their existing separate alerts.
